acceptance_criteria: AC-1 On an empty local_credentials table, first boot creates exactly two identities and no more.
AC-2 On a table holding any row, first boot creates nothing and changes nothing.

AC-3 THE DECISIVE TEST: change a password, run the seeding routine again, and assert the changed password still authenticates and the documented initial one does not. Observed to FAIL against a naive always-seed implementation before the fix.
AC-4 The partially-seeded case is decided explicitly and tested, not left to fall out of the code.
AC-5 A test asserts no documented initial password and no verifier literal appears in the tracked tree outside documentation prose.
AC-6 Seeding produces one audit_log row per identity, attributed to the reserved bootstrap marker, carrying no credential material.
AC-7 First boot creates no role_bindings row; a test asserts the table is still empty afterwards.
AC-8 ui2/cli's bootstrap-local-identity still works and has a test.
AC-9 ./ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build -x :integration-tests:test passes, :service:test passes, architecture tests pass, module listing still eleven.
AC-10 The repository privacy gate reports zero findings.
AC-11 No file under panorama/, configuration/, utils/, scripts/ or docs/design/ is modified.

A test proving a restart cannot reset a changed password, observed failing before the fix.
SESSION_CLOSE naming which BOOT clause each type implements, what was decided for the partially-seeded case, and the test counts before and after.

recommended_reasoning.reason: Small diff, but it is a credential-seeding path where the obvious implementation carries a real defect: unconditional seeding silently restores a documented password over a changed one. High effort for the care, and because the partially-seeded case needs a decision rather than an accident.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every public type and method carries a short comment naming the contract clause it implements.
Write the BOOT-2 test FIRST and confirm it fails against a naive always-seed implementation, then implement. Report both observations in the SESSION_CLOSE. A test never seen to fail proves nothing.
Do NOT use './ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build' without '-x :integration-tests:test'; the integration tests fail closed on a missing database by design.
Do not run the full Python pytest suite; it creates untracked data/ and logs/ directories the privacy gate then flags.
The ui2 build must keep exactly eleven Gradle subprojects.
Do not merge to main. The Product Owner assistant reviews the diff and merges.
If the contract does not answer something, raise one RELAY_QUESTION rather than deciding it.
risks: Seeding unconditionally, so a restart silently restores a documented credential over an operator's changed password. This is the defect BOOT-2 exists to prevent and AC-3 is the test for it.
Putting the verifier in a migration, which pins the random salt in version control and turns a documented default into a precomputed one.
Creating a role_bindings row because the accounts look useless without one. C3 keeps that CLI-only and fail-closed.
Letting the initial password reach a log line or an exception message.
Breaking the existing CLI path while adding the automatic one.

in: BOOT-1: on service startup, when local_credentials holds NO rows, create exactly two identities, nexusadmin and claudeadmin, with their documented initial passwords. When the table holds any row, do nothing at all.

BOOT-2, and this is the decisive rule: the empty-table condition exists so a restart can never reset a password an operator has changed. Implement the check so that it cannot be defeated by a partially-seeded table either -- decide and state what happens when the table holds one row but not the other, rather than leaving it to fall out of the code.

BOOT-3: compute each verifier at boot using the existing Argon2 hasher and its per-credential random salt. NO migration, source file, resource or manifest may contain a password or a precomputed verifier. The initial password is a documented constant in the contract; its verifier must never be a literal anywhere in the tree.

BOOT-4: each created identity produces an audit_log row through C1 section 3.5's existing trigger, attributed to a reserved bootstrap actor marker -- the same posture C3's own bootstrap clause already uses for role binding. No credential material may reach the row.

BOOT-5: create IDENTITIES only. Create no role_bindings row. C3's Bootstrap clause keeps the first role:security_admin binding a CLI-only, deployment-controlled action and this movement does not touch it. A freshly deployed product must be able to authenticate and have no authorization until the deployment step runs.
Keep ui2/cli's existing bootstrap-local-identity action working. It is the deployment-controlled path and BOOT-1 is additive to it, not a replacement.

Tests for contract section 4's acceptance, including the decisive one: change a password, restart the seeding routine, and assert the CHANGED password still authenticates while the documented initial one does not.
A test that greps the tracked tree and asserts neither documented initial password nor any verifier literal appears outside documentation prose.
out: Creating any role_bindings row, or changing C3's Bootstrap clause in any way.
Any forced password change, password expiry, complexity, history or reuse rule. The Product Owner deferred password policy on 2026-09-13.
Changing credential storage, login, lockout, password change or the constant-cost verification -- all frozen in C3A and already implemented.

Editing any existing Flyway migration. If a migration is needed at all, it is additive; prefer application-side seeding, since BOOT-3 forbids a verifier literal and a migration is where one would end up.
Changing sessions, RBAC evaluation or the gate chain.
Any user-management screen, any LDAP/RADIUS/TACACS work, any device contact, any discovery work.
Anything under panorama/, configuration/, utils/ or scripts/.
